A 50-year-old man is hospitalized with extensive hematomas in the right pectoral and axillary regions
(20 x 7 cm), right hemiabdomen (30 x 30 cm), and left lumbar area (25 x 5 cm). He has a history of
progressive malignant prostate disease and underwent surgery for it a few months ago. He reports no
subjective symptoms. His vital signs are as follows: temperature 37ºC (98.6ºF), pulse 74/min,
respirations 13/min, and blood pressure 125/72 mm Hg. On examination, both knee joints are swollen
and tender. Laboratory results reveal: - Hematocrit: 39% - Bleeding time: 11 minutes - Platelet count:
280,000/mm³ - Partial thromboplastin time: 64 seconds - Prothrombin time: 19 seconds - Fibrinogen
level: 1.068 g/L - D-dimer assay: 1.122 mg/L What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A)
Vitamin K deficiency (B) Factor XIII deficiency (C) Liver disease coagulopathy (D) Classic von
Willebrand disease (E) Secondary hyperfibrinolysis (F) Hemophilia A (G) Disseminated intravascular
coagulation (DIC) (H) Acquired factor VIII inhibitor (I) Antiphospholipid syndrome (J) Primary
hyperfibrinolysis
 A. Primary hyperfibrinolysis
B. Classic von Willebrand disease
C. Acquired factor VIII inhibitor
D. Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
E. Factor XIII deficiency
F. Secondary hyperfibrinolysis
G. Vitamin K deficiency
H. Antiphospholipid syndrome
I. Hemophilia A
J. Liver disease coagulopathy
